transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-10-28
Start time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Daniel (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood CSM), Evan (SB Eng), Sara (SB InfoSec), Tom (SB DevOps), Lina (SB Product), Ben (SB Legal)

Summary: Weekly POC security sync focusing on SSO, audit logs/retention, SOC2 artifacts, and any blockers. Reviewed a small set of recent logs from the pilot, discussed RBAC patterns, KMS integration options, and compliance packaging. Agreed on next steps around sharing SOC2 attestation, sample audit exports, and scheduling technical deep-dive for SAML/KMS.

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, happy Tuesday. quick roll call?
[00:07] Evan: Evan here.
[00:09] Sara: Sara — InfoSec.
[00:10] Tom: Tom, DevOps.
[00:12] Lina: Lina, product.
[00:13] Ben: Ben, legal.
[00:15] Maya: Great. I'll kick it off—this is our weekly POC security sync for the Southbridge pilot. agenda is SSO, audit logs/retention, SOC2 artifacts, and any blockers. Daniel, anything you want to call out from the infra side before we dive in?
[00:28] Daniel: Yeah quick note—last week we pushed the log export hook from the Dedicated nodes to your splunk cluster in staging, there was a little formatting mismatch, looks like timestamp fields were missing timezone. We've patched the exporter but wanted to confirm your ingestion schema.
[00:41] Tom: Right — we saw events but tz was off, caused some search misses. we'll share our ingestion spec after this meeting. also curious about the level of detail in the audit logs, like do we get per-token traces or just per-request metadata?
[00:55] Daniel: Good question. by default Redwood emits per-request metadata and event types: request-start, model-select, response-end, error. we can enable more verbose KV cache events or token-level sampling but that increases volume. currently the sample we sent had request-id, user-id (pseudonymized in the sample), model, latency, and error codes.
[01:16] Sara: Two quick compliance asks—1) we need assurance on log integrity and tamper evidence, like append-only or signed logs; 2) retention policy, we have a baseline 7 years for some financial traces, but for pilot maybe we start with 3 months and scope upward. how does Redwood support retention and legal-hold?
[01:35] Priya: For hosted we have configurable retention windows and can export archived logs to a customer S3 bucket. For Dedicated or Private deployments you can point audit exports to your own storage and apply lifecycle policies. we also support signed audit logs via our audit service; i will include the technical note in the security pack.
[01:51] Maya: Also to add, we support push-based delivery to your SIEM — the exported files can be gzipped and checksums included.
[01:58] Ben: On the legal side, we need a formal attestation that Redwood preserves chain-of-custody for those logs and a copy of SOC2 Type II. is that something you can provide?
[02:10] Maya: yes, absolutely. we'll send the SOC2 Type II, plus a short attestation note. i'll be the point for that.
[02:16] Ben: Thanks.
[02:18] Lina: quick product note — we saw a couple of hallucination examples in the end-to-end tests. not security-specific but wanted to flag as it ties to redaction and PII handling when responses include patient/customer-like text. what's the PII redaction model?
[02:33] Daniel: There's a couple options. we can enable pre-response redaction hooks where the runtime will scrub any detected PII tokens using regex and ML detectors. alternatively, you can route responses through a post-processing lambda to do domain-specific redaction. both are supported in the pilot but we haven't turned it on by default.
[02:50] Sara: We prefer in-runtime redaction so it's consistent and provable, but we need to see false-negative rates. can you provide stats or an evaluation?
[02:59] Daniel: I can pull our internal evals for common US SSN/email/phone patterns; caveat, pattern-based rules do better on structured PII, ML detectors catch fuzzy PII but have some FN. i'll attach a short eval snapshot.
[03:12] Evan: Back to SSO — our timeline is tight, we want SAML now, OIDC later. do you have a SAML metadata import process? and how's SP vs IdP flow handled?
[03:25] Maya: We support both SAML and OIDC. For SAML we can import metadata XML or configure via the console. typical flow: you register Redwood as a service provider, exchange certs, and we propagate assertions to the console RBAC. Daniel, maybe you can outline the RBAC mapping?
[03:40] Daniel: Sure. we map SAML attributes to roles in the console; you can enforce role-based restrictions for routes (e.g., only Legal can see audit exports, only Ops can spin up private jobs). we also have session timeout and MFA hints you can enforce via IdP.
[03:53] Tom: For Dedicated, can the SSO be proxied through our internal AD FS? we don't want traffic to go outside for auth assertions.
[04:02] Daniel: Yes for Private deployments you can use internal IdP endpoints — SAML assertions are brokered within your VPC. For Hosted we do standard SP-initiated flows, but if you need IdP-initiated or AD FS via VPN we can design a pattern.
[04:17] Sara: On KMS—we need BYOK (bring-your-own-key) with an HSM-backed provider. which providers are supported and how is envelope encryption handled?
[04:27] Priya: We support AWS KMS, Google KMS, Azure Key Vault, and customers can also provide HSM-managed keys via our Private deployments. envelope encryption is used for model artifacts and cached KV; keys are never stored unencrypted in our control plane. we'll include the key-handling doc.
[04:44] Ben: Any audit on key rotation policies? we need to ensure older keys can be revoked and past logs remain decryptable if within retention.
[04:52] Daniel: Rotation is supported via key aliases — we keep metadata about which key encrypted which blob; decryption uses the referenced key alias and fallback if rotated. full details and limitations will be in the KMS integration guide.
[05:07] Lina: We had a short test where an engineer saw tokens in logs that looked like raw prompt text. is there a way to avoid storing raw prompts in plaintext?
[05:17] Daniel: By default we do not log full prompt text in hosted exports; the pilot sample had a debug flag turned on that included prompt snippets — that's our bad. we will sanitize—there's a config toggle 'redwood.log.prompt_text=false'. we'll re-send a sanitized sample.
[05:33] Sara: Good to know. also need clarification on redaction at rest vs in-transit — what protections exist for your export buckets?
[05:42] Priya: Exports to S3 can be encrypted server-side or client-side with your KMS keys. in transit we use TLS 1.2+; also we can enable mutual TLS on S3 endpoints for extra assurance.
[05:55] Evan: we have a question about audit trails for admin actions in the Redwood console — if someone revokes a key or changes retention, do we have a tamper-evident trail with user, timestamp, IP?
[06:08] Daniel: Yes admin actions are recorded with user, role, action, timestamp, and IP. those records can be exported and fed to your SIEM. the records are append-only and we include a checksum chain per day to detect tampering.
[06:21] Sara: can you show a sample audit log line? even a mocked one.
[06:25] Priya: i'll attach a sample in the security pack but quick example: {timestamp, request_id, user_email, action: 'retention.update', old_value: '90d', new_value: '365d', ip: 'x.x.x.x'}. note: actual field names might vary slightly in the export.
[06:43] Ben: for contract language around breach notification, what's your SLA for notifying customers if there's a suspicious access to audit logs or key compromise?
[06:52] Maya: We follow our standard incident response SLAs in the draft contract — notify within 72 hours for region-impacting events; for critical key compromise we escalate immediately and provide playbook. we'll surface the exact language in the next contract iteration.
[07:06] Tom: Are there rate limits on how often we can pull audit exports? we might want near-real-time streaming to Splunk.
[07:13] Daniel: We support streaming via webhook or Kinesis—near real-time is possible; heavy sampling will have an egress cost, but functionally it's supported.
[07:23] Sara: any limitations on queryability when logs are exported to S3 vs when they remain in Redwood's internal store?
[07:30] Daniel: In Redwood's store you get query APIs and retained indices for 90 days by default; exported S3 objects are raw events and you'd need to index them into your SIEM. we can optionally provide pre-indexed parquet exports for faster ingestion.
[07:47] Evan: okay, let's talk deliverables. we need SOC2 Type II, sample audit export, sanitized logs, SAML metadata template, and KMS integration guide. can we get all of that in the next week?
[08:00] Maya: we'll prioritize. i'll take SOC2 and high-level attestation. Priya will take the sample logs and sanitized export. Daniel will do SAML/KMS docs and we'll target sending the bundle by 2025-11-03.
[08:12] Lina: in parallel, can we get a short run of the redaction eval on a small prompt corpus specific to finance data?
[08:20] Daniel: yes we can run a domain-specific eval but need a sanitized corpus from you, or we can use synthetic prompts that mimic your patterns. if you can share a small sample dataset (sanitized) i can run the redaction test next week.
[08:33] Sara: we'll prepare a sanitized set — maybe 200 rows — and ship it. confidentiality note: it'll be under NDA.
[08:40] Ben: legal wants to confirm the NDA scope covers logs and audit exports.
[08:43] Maya: understood — we'll mark that in the security pack and coordinate with your legal.
[08:47] Evan: any outstanding blockers from Redwood side?
[08:50] Priya: only the corrected sanitized log sample — we noticed the pilot had debug prompts enabled. once we turn that off and resend, it should align.
[08:59] Daniel: minor: we need Tom's KMS provider info (AWS/Azure/GCP or HSM vendor) to validate key wrapping.
[09:07] Tom: i'll send that in a follow-up email.
[09:10] Maya: great — recap of next steps: SOC2 + attestation by 2025-11-03, sample sanitized audit exports by 2025-11-04, SAML/KMS deep dive scheduled week of 2025-11-10, redaction eval pending sanitized corpus from Southbridge. any other items?
[09:30] Lina: just one: can we enable a demo of the audit-export import into our Splunk dev environment? a quick pairing session would help.
[09:38] Daniel: yes we can schedule a pairing import session after we send the sample — propose 2025-11-06 for the Splunk pairing?
[09:45] Sara: that works for us.
[09:47] Maya: excellent. thanks everyone. we'll follow up in email with the security pack link and attach the sample audit export.
[09:55] Evan: thanks all, bye.

Notes:
- There were minor transcription artifacts: sometimes product names were 'Redwood Dedicated' vs 'Dedicated nodes' and 'KV cache' was spoken quickly and transcribed as 'k v cache'.
- References to artifacts to be shared: (1) 'Redwood_security_pack_v2.pdf' (link to be sent), (2) sample-audit-export-2025-10-27.json (sanitized), (3) SAML-metadata-template.xml, (4) redaction-eval-summary.xlsx.

Explicit next steps / deliverables (reiterated):
- Redwood (Maya): Share SOC2 Type II attestation and security pack (target 2025-11-03).
- Redwood (Priya): Provide sanitized sample audit export + schema (target 2025-11-04).
- Redwood (Daniel): SAML/SOAP? (SAML) integration guide, KMS key handling doc, and run redaction eval once corpus provided (target docs by 2025-11-04; eval next week).
- Southbridge (Tom/Sara): Provide KMS provider and sanitized corpus for redaction eval (target 2025-11-05).

End of transcript.
